correctness.rationale: All parameters are positive and p is arbitrary finite. The map has a unique attracting strictly positive equilibrium by positive Perron root >1, bounded monotone iterations and strict subhomogeneity. The closed-form candidate gives equal derivatives \(t^2\), and the conservation equation is the quadratic-root identity \(C=B(t+t^{-1})\). A positive rank-one matrix realizes it. Exact fraction algebra gives a positive tangent remainder with equality exactly at the constructed profile; summation proves the stated global deficit for any positive conservative D. The independent carrying-vector comparison proves strict improvement iff growth rates are not all equal. The (p−1)^2 dimension follows from independent linear constraints. Verification: exact Q(sqrt5) sample and 780 reproducible numerical configurations with random matrices and rank-one optimizers. Those finite checks corroborate, not replace, the universal proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 study identifies enhancing versus diminishing dispersal, yet practical patch connectivity design asks how large equilibrium population can become over every permitted redistribution. The analytic optimum for arbitrary p, a simple one-step construction, all-optimizer affine dimension, sharp iff growth heterogeneity criterion, and exact nonnegative loss identity form a meaningful structural classification, stronger than routine numerical improvement or a special-case sign check. This precisely quantifies the effect of spatial mismatch from optimal pre-growth allocation; it does not assume a general ecological management benefit when migration is costly or constrained.
